data.name: Kateb
data.gender_notes: Kateb is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who records, documents, or writes. A person of knowledge, wisdom, and high moral character. The name Kateb carries the meaning “Scribe, Writer” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Kateb usually hope their child will grow to embody scribe, writer and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: May your name be synonymous with knowledge, wisdom, and righteousness.
data.etymology: Kateb belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Scribe, Writer.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kateb total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_english.name: Kateb
in_english.meaning: One who writes, records, or documents
in_english.long_meaning: Derived from Arabic root 'k-t-b' meaning to write or record, significant name in Islamic tradition symbolizing a person of knowledge and wisdom, historically known as scribes or writers who copied sacred texts and important documents

data.cultural_impact: The name Kateb has cultural significance as it is derived from the Arabic word 'kidxb', meaning 'writer' or 'recorder'. This name holds prestige in Islamic culture as people associated with learning, education, and high moral character are often referred to as 'katebs'. They were traditional scribes, copyists, scholars, teachers, bibliophiles or calligraphers, who dedicated their lives to the preservation of knowledge. The title was also given to judges, record keepers, and in some cases, to secretaries of caliphs. Many great scholars in Islamic history bore this name, and it continues to be a respected designation in contemporary Muslim societies.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Kateb also holds spiritual significance as it represents a person of knowledge and wisdom. In Islamic tradition, knowledge is highly valued and considered a means to drawing closer to God. As the Holy Quran states, "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding." (3:190). By being a "kateb", an individual embodies this trait of seeking, documenting, and preserving knowledge, fulfilling this spiritual requirement, and connecting to the divine through the pursuit of wisdom.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Scribe, Writer" symbolizes One who records, documents, or writes. A person of knowledge, wisdom, and high moral character.. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Kateb serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of scribe, writer.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abi Maryam al-Qayrawani (d. 956 AD) was a prominent scholar in the Fatimid Caliphate. He was also known as Ibn Kateb due to his excellent handwriting. The term 'kateb' in Arabic means 'one who writes'.
historical_references.context: Ibn Kateb was a prominent scholar and calligrapher.

historical_references.reference: Imam Al-Hakim (r. 996-1021 AD) was a Fatimid Caliph known as 'Al-Kateb billah' which translates to 'God's Scribe'. He was given this title due to his extensive knowledge and his role as a scribe for the religious texts.
historical_references.context: Al-Kateb billah was a Fatimid Caliph and a scholar known for his extensive knowledge and his role as a scribe for religious texts.

name_in_real_life.story: A successful entrepreneur named Aisha Kateb in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia attributes much of their success to the blessing of their name Kateb, which means "Scribe, Writer". They believe their name has shaped their identity and guided them through life.
